item.title: Sprint b-9 — neutral tests, docs and API text, health, and the lint gate (WP-7, WP-8, WP-10)

results.statement: The bdc CLI must offer two command surfaces: a beads surface shaped like the bd /v0 interface, and a separate cache-management surface.
results.quote: The bdc CLI must offer two command surfaces: a beads surface shaped like the bd /v0 interface, and a separate cache-management surface.
results.deterministic_check: contract.md section 1 lists both groups; bdc --help shows the beads and cache command groups

criteria.no: The item is about another part of the system, such as storage internals, scheduling, CI lint or release packaging, and does not add, change, lay out, document or test any bdc command or bd-cache-api request.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether any bdc command or bd-cache-api request is involved.
criteria.yes: The item is about at least one bdc command, flag, help text or command group, the bdc command layout (including creating the bdc binary or its entry point), or a bd-cache-api request.

relevant.instructions: Does the work in `item.text` concern the commands of the `bdc` CLI or the bd-cache-api request vocabulary: adding, renaming, removing, moving, changing, laying out, keeping, documenting or testing a bdc command, subcommand, flag, help text or command group, or a bd-cache-api request? Judge only whether the item is about these things, not whether it handles them correctly.

criteria.no: The item does not state the structure or place its commands in it: it is silent about the bd /v0 shape and the separate cache group, mentions command surfaces or CLI consistency only as a topic, names the anchor only by its id, or plans some other command structure.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions bd compatibility or a cache group, but it cannot be determined whether its commands keep the bd /v0 shape or the separate cache group.
criteria.yes: The item states the two-surface structure, or explicitly says that its beads command matches bd /v0 (wording such as same name, flags or output as bd, mirrors bd, stands in for bd, bd-compatible), or explicitly says that its cache command stays in the separate cache-management group.

addressed.instructions: The anchor requires `bdc` to keep two command surfaces: (1) a beads surface whose commands are shaped like the bd /v0 interface, meaning the same command names, flags and output as `bd`; and (2) a separate cache-management surface, such as a `bdc cache` group, kept apart from the beads commands. Does `item.text` explicitly state this two-surface structure, or, for the commands it adds or changes, explicitly place them in it: a beads command shaped like bd /v0, or a cache-management command in the separate cache group? Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: The item plans none of the breaking changes. Silence about the surfaces, or a command whose group is not stated, is not a break.
criteria.unclear: The item plans a change to the command layout but it cannot be told whether it merges the surfaces or moves beads commands away from bd /v0.
criteria.yes: The item plans at least one of the breaking changes: a merged or flat command list, no separate cache group, beads commands or flags renamed away from bd /v0, or cache commands moved among the beads commands.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something that breaks the two-surface structure in `anchor.statement`? Breaking it means any of: merging the cache-management commands into the beads commands or into one flat list; removing the separate cache group; renaming beads commands or flags away from bd /v0 or dropping bd compatibility; placing cache-management commands among the bd-shaped beads commands. An item that is silent about the surfaces, or adds a command without saying where it goes, does not break it. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: beads-cache must run its sync of bd, the beads issue-tracker CLI, at the times set in a SQLite cron table.
results.quote: beads-cache needs to handle the synchronization of bd on a cron tick. [...] long term sync would be done by beads-cache at a time scheduled in the cron scheduler in sqlite cron table.
results.context: phase-b planning session, 2026-10-25 (Rand); wording by bc-lead under Rand's instruction to use judgement
results.deterministic_check: a test runs the built-in sync from an sc-cron schedule row in the cache file

criteria.no: The item's work does not involve the bd sync: it is about another part of the system, such as packaging, release channels, documentation, or a scheduled job other than the bd sync.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions syncing or scheduling, but it is not possible to tell whether the bd sync is meant.
criteria.yes: The item schedules, runs, triggers, configures or changes the bd sync (the tick), for example its schedule row, its scopes or filters, its hooks, or a command that runs it.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor (`anchor.statement`, `anchor.scope`) about the bd sync: beads-cache's job that syncs issues from bd, the beads issue-tracker CLI, into the cache. The bd sync is also called the tick, as in `bdc cache tick` or `bd_cache_sync::tick`. Does the work in `item.text` schedule, run, trigger, configure or change the bd sync? Judge only whether the item's work involves the bd sync. Do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item does not say the bd sync runs from a SQLite cron table: it is silent about when the sync runs, says only that a schedule is needed or will be decided later, names a different source of times, or is not about the bd sync.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a cron table or a schedule near the bd sync, but it cannot be told whether the bd sync's times come from a SQLite cron table.
criteria.yes: The item says the bd sync runs at the times set by a row or entry in a SQLite cron table kept by beads-cache, such as sc-cron's table in the cache file.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires one specific thing: the bd sync runs at the times set in a SQLite cron table that beads-cache keeps. Does `item.text` say this: that the bd sync's schedule is a row or entry in a SQLite cron table (for example sc-cron's cron table, job table or schedule table in the cache file) and that the sync runs at the times that row sets? Judge only whether this specific content is present. Do not judge whether anything in the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item rules out running the bd sync at the times set in a SQLite cron table, whether or not the item mentions it.
criteria.unclear: The item describes how the bd sync is triggered, but it cannot be told whether that excludes the SQLite cron table.
criteria.yes: The item plans a schedule, trigger or design for the bd sync that cannot be reconciled with running it at the times set in a SQLite cron table.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires beads-cache to run its bd sync at the times set in a SQLite cron table. Does `item.text` plan something that rules this out? Conflicts include: the sync runs only when an external scheduler (OS cron, systemd, launchd, Task Scheduler, CI) invokes a command; the sync's times come from somewhere other than a SQLite cron table, such as a fixed timer or an interval in a config file; the cache keeps no schedule of its own. These are not conflicts: silence about scheduling; a command that runs one extra sync on demand while the schedule stays in the cron table; letting a consumer disable the built-in sync row or run its own sync method instead. Judge conflict only.

results.context: phase-b planning session, 2026-10-25 (Rand); wording by bc-lead under Rand's instruction to use judgement
results.deterministic_check: an end-to-end test disables the built-in sync row and a registered Python sync ingests a scope

criteria.no: No part of the item is about that sync; the item concerns another area of the project.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to syncing in passing and it is not possible to tell whether its work is about the sync.
criteria.yes: At least one part of the item is about the sync that copies bd issues into the cache, as listed in the instructions.

relevant.instructions: `anchor.statement` is about which code performs the sync that copies bd issues into beads-cache: the built-in bd sync, or a sync method the consumer registers. Is any part of `item.text` about that sync: the built-in sync job, when or whether it runs, a consumer's own sync, what happens before or after a sync, or how synced rows are ingested? Judge topic only.

criteria.no: The item has no planned step in which a consumer's registered Python method takes over the sync from the built-in bd sync. Disabling the built-in sync alone, post-sync hooks, sync documentation or status calls, a cited anchor ID, a non-Python replacement, and statements that replacement is impossible are all no.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a consumer-supplied sync but it is not possible to tell whether it takes over from the built-in sync.
criteria.yes: The item says a consumer can register a Python sync method (function, callable, or sync row) that runs as the sync instead of the built-in bd sync, for example after the built-in row is disabled or switched off.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for a consumer-registered Python sync method to replace the hard-coded bd sync, as `anchor.statement` requires? Judge presence of that replacement only.

criteria.no: The item says none of those things. It may not mention the replacement, may plan only part of it (such as disabling the built-in sync), may add hooks that run before or after the built-in sync, or may plan the replacement itself.
criteria.unclear: The item limits the sync or its replacement in a way that may or may not exclude a consumer Python sync.
criteria.yes: The item says the built-in sync cannot be disabled or replaced, that consumers cannot register their own sync, that the built-in sync is the only sync, or that only non-Python replacements are allowed.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` rule out what `anchor.statement` requires: a consumer-registered Python sync method replacing the hard-coded bd sync? Judge conflict only. Silence about the replacement is not a conflict, and neither is work that keeps, schedules, documents, or adds hooks around the built-in sync.

results.statement: beads-cache must support an optional consumer-registered post-sync hook that receives the bd sync results and errors.
results.quote: there can also be hooks necessary to report/escelate based on [the first consumer's] requirements [...] We would also likely want a 'post-sync' hook that could contain sync results and errors and allow consumer [the first consumer] to do custom things at that point (Rand, 2026-10-25, paraphrased; the verbatim text is in git history)
results.context: phase-b planning session, 2026-10-25 (Rand); wording by bc-lead under Rand's instruction to use judgement
results.deterministic_check: an end-to-end test asserts the post-sync hook request carries each scope's result and error

criteria.no: The item's work is elsewhere: it only calls the sync without changing it (for example a CLI command that runs the tick), it handles write-journal escalation, or it is about something unrelated such as packaging or a git hook.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether its work is in (a), (b) or (c).
criteria.yes: The item builds, changes, removes or defers something in (a), (b) or (c).

relevant.instructions: Does the work in `item.text` build, change, remove or defer any of these: (a) the bd sync job itself (the built-in sync, also called the tick: its code, schedule or scopes, or a consumer's own replacement sync); (b) how bd sync failures are reported or escalated; (c) what runs after a bd sync finishes, such as hooks or callbacks and the sync results and errors they receive? An item whose only contact with the sync is calling it, for example a CLI command that runs the tick and prints its reply, is not in these areas. Escalating write-journal entries, for example refusals found when the journal is flushed, is not escalation of sync failures. Judge only whether the item's work is in (a), (b) or (c), not whether it provides the hook in `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item plans no such hook, or one that does not receive both, or defers it out of this plan.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to a hook after the sync but it is not possible to tell what it receives.
criteria.yes: The item plans a hook run after the sync that receives both the sync results and the sync errors.

addressed.instructions: Look in `item.text` for a planned hook that runs after a bd sync and receives two things: the results of that sync and its errors. Words such as callback or handler count for the hook, outcomes or per-scope status for the results, and failures for the errors. A hook that gets only one of the two, a general promise of hooks, or a hook moved out of this plan does not count. Judge only whether the item plans this hook.

criteria.no: The item decides nothing against those properties, including an item that never mentions the hook.
criteria.unclear: The item makes a decision about hooks or sync outcomes whose effect on those properties cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item decides against one of the four properties (for example a hook that must be registered, a hook skipped when the sync fails, or results and errors kept only in a reply or log with no hook) or decides the hook will not exist in this plan.

contradicted.instructions: The hook required by `anchor.statement` has four properties: it is optional, a consumer can register it, it is called after the bd sync, and it receives the sync results and errors. Does `item.text` decide against any of these properties, or decide that the hook will not exist in this plan? Silence about the hook is not deciding against it. Removing beads-cache's own escalation is not deciding against it, because escalation belongs in the consumer's hook. Judge conflict only.

criteria.unclear: The item mentions scopes, but the text is too vague to tell whether the work defines, parses, or syncs them.

relevant.instructions: Does the work in `item.text` define, parse, configure, store, or sync beads-cache sync scopes, or change the code that does? A sync scope is the unit the bd sync selects beads by. Removing or replacing an existing way of defining scopes also counts. Judge whether the item touches sync scopes only; do not judge whether it follows `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item does not contain the bd filter definition of a sync scope.
criteria.unclear: The item contains wording close to the definition, but it cannot be told whether it says scopes are bd filters.
criteria.yes: The item contains the bd filter definition of a sync scope in one of the acceptable wordings.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that sync scopes be defined as bd filters. Does `item.text` contain that definition as a plan, step, or constraint, in any wording? Acceptable wording includes: bd filter, `bd list` arguments or flags, label filter, label query, `--label`, `--all`. A statement only about the topic of scopes, without saying they are bd filters, does not count. Judge presence only, not conflict.

criteria.no: Every scope the item defines is a bd filter, or the item does not say how scopes are defined, or it removes phase-based scopes.
criteria.unclear: The item says how scopes are chosen in words that could mean either a bd filter or a phase, and the text does not settle which.
criteria.yes: The item defines, reads, or selects at least one sync scope by phase or by another means that is not a bd filter, including as a fallback or default.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` define, read, or select a sync scope in a way that is not a bd filter, for example from phase files, a phase registry, an active-phase rule, or open phase epic or root beads, including as a fallback or default? Removing or replacing phase-based scopes is not a conflict. A bd label whose name contains the word phase is still a bd filter. Silence about how scopes are defined is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.unclear: The item mentions the store's tables or indexes but it is not possible to tell whether it plans any work on their definitions.

relevant.instructions: The anchor in `anchor.statement` governs the table and index definitions of the beads-cache store file. Does `item.text` plan work on those definitions, that is, an edit of `crates/bd-cache-store/src/schema.rs` or any addition, removal or change of a store table, column or index? Only overlap of subject matter is judged here: whether the change is permitted is a separate question.

criteria.no: `item.text` does not write the constraint down: it is silent, it only lists the store change it makes, it only names the store schema or v3 tables as a topic, or it is about other work.
criteria.unclear: `item.text` states some limit on its store work but it is not possible to tell whether that limit is this constraint.
criteria.yes: `item.text` writes the constraint down, in its own words: the v3 tables and indexes are kept as they are, or the store work only adds nullable columns or new tables.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` sets one constraint: the store file's v3 tables and indexes stay unchanged, and only nullable columns and new tables may be added. Is that constraint itself written down in `item.text`, as a stated rule, guarantee or limit on the item's store work? The item's planned change alone, the topic of the store schema, or the word 'v3' alone is not the constraint being written down. Do not decide whether the item obeys or breaks the constraint.

criteria.no: Carrying out the item would only add nullable columns or new tables, or would leave the store schema alone, including when the item never mentions it.
criteria.unclear: The item changes an existing store table or index in a way it does not describe well enough to tell whether the rule is broken.
criteria.yes: Carrying out the item would rename, drop or retype a v3 table or column, add a NOT NULL column, or drop, rename or alter a v3 index.

contradicted.instructions: Would carrying out the plan in `item.text` break the rule in `anchor.statement` that the store's v3 tables and indexes stay unchanged, with only nullable columns and new tables added? Break the rule: rename, drop or retype a v3 table or column; add a column that is NOT NULL; drop, rename or alter a v3 index. Keep the rule: add a nullable column to any table, add a new table, or leave the store schema alone. If the item does not mention the store schema, it keeps the rule. Judge only whether the plan breaks the rule.
